era: Off-road motocross and ATV racing crossover
summary: Rainbow Studios' MX/ATV crossover series, joining motocross bikes, ATVs, and broader off-road vehicles across THQ and THQ Nordic eras.

entries.title: MX vs. ATV Unleashed
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC release plus PSP On the Edge for exclusive portable areas

emulation.notes: Use Windows as primary; PPSSPP preserves On the Edge.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC route exceeds original console/portable fidelity

primary.why: MX vs. ATV Unleashed released on PlayStation 2, Xbox, Windows, mobile phones, and PSP as MX vs. ATV: On the Edge. The Windows version is the highest-fidelity route and adds a track editor, while the PSP port has some extra areas but loses aircraft from the console/PC game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC version for the main game and track editor; use the PSP On the Edge port separately if preserving its extra areas.

secondary.version: MX vs. ATV: On the Edge
secondary.why: The PSP port adds several playable areas but lacks the aircraft available in the console/PC edition.
secondary.how_to_play: Play with PPSSPP or original PSP hardware after the Windows primary route.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release with higher fidelity and a track editor.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity route with an exclusive editor.
skip: console route and no content advantage over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release with online support historically available on Xbox Live.
all_releases.reason: skip: console route and no content advantage over Windows for offline preservation.
skip: reduced mobile route and no sourced content advantage over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Portable On the Edge port with extra areas but missing aircraft from the main version.
all_releases.reason: secondary: preserves PSP-exclusive areas after the Windows route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows has higher fidelity and the track editor, while PSP On the Edge adds areas but removes aircraft, so the PSP port is secondary rather than primary.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster; original online services have changed, with replacement-server support documented for original Xbox online play.

entries.title: MX vs. ATV Untamed

emulation.emulator: Xenia / RPCS3 / PCSX2 / Dolphin / PPSSPP / melonDS
emulation.notes: Use Xenia or original Xbox 360 hardware for the primary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: HD console fidelity with emulator upscaling

primary.why: Untamed released across PlayStation 2, PlayStation 3, PSP, Xbox 360, Wii, Nintendo DS, and mobile phones. With no PC version, the Xbox 360 release is a high-fidelity HD console route for the full home-console game, while handheld/mobile versions are reduced or divergent access routes.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 release on original hardware or Xenia; use other platforms only for preservation of control/platform differences.

all_releases.reason: primary: high-fidelity home-console route.
skip: comparable console route and no sourced content advantage over Xbox 360.
skip: lower-fidelity route and no sourced content advantage over Xbox 360.

entries.title: MX vs. ATV Reflex

emulation.emulator: Native Windows / RPCS3 / Xenia / PPSSPP / melonDS
emulation.notes: Use the native Windows version as primary; emulate console/portable versions only for preservation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC route exceeds original console/portable fidelity

primary.why: Reflex released on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, PSP, and Nintendo DS. The Windows and HD console versions preserve the physics, Rider Reflex controls, terrain deformation, local split-screen, and online events; Windows is the highest-fidelity configurable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC version at the highest stable settings; use PS3/Xbox 360 only as console alternatives and handheld versions only for preservation.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release with configurable fidelity, Rider Reflex controls, real-time terrain deformation, local split-screen, and online event support.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity configurable route.

entries.title: MX vs. ATV Alive

emulation.notes: Use Xenia or original Xbox 360 hardware for the primary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: HD console fidelity with emulator upscaling

primary.version: Original Xbox 360 release with DLC where owned
primary.why: Alive released only on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. The game was built around a lower-price base release with substantial paid DLC, so the Xbox 360 route with owned DLC installed is the recommended preservation route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 release on original hardware or Xenia with owned DLC installed; use PS3 as the alternate console route.

all_releases.fidelity: HD console release; install owned DLC to preserve the intended expanded content set.
all_releases.reason: primary: high-fidelity console route with DLC where owned.
skip: comparable console route and no sourced content advantage over Xbox 360.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced PS3-exclusive content requires a secondary route; completeness depends on owned DLC on either console.

entries.remaster_caveats: The base game intentionally shipped with less content and more paid DLC than prior entries; install owned DLC for the fullest route.

entries.title: MX vs. ATV Supercross / Supercross Encore
entries.definitive_edition: MX vs. ATV Supercross Encore on Windows

emulation.notes: Use the native Windows Encore version as primary; emulate original console versions only for preservation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC Encore route exceeds original console fidelity

primary.why: MX vs. ATV Supercross first released on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, then received the updated Supercross Encore release on Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One. Encore adds later-platform support and new features, while the game includes 17 Supercross tracks, career series, more than 80 motocross companies, 40 riders, split-screen, and online multiplayer up to 12 players; Windows Encore is the best route.
primary.how_to_play: Play MX vs. ATV Supercross Encore on Windows at the highest stable settings; use PS4 or Xbox One Encore as console alternatives.

all_releases.fidelity: Updated Encore PC release with later-platform features and configurable fidelity.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most complete updated route.
skip: earlier route superseded by Encore for best-version play.
skip: earlier route superseded by Encore for best-version play.
skip: console route and no sourced content advantage over Windows Encore.
skip: console route and no sourced content advantage over Windows Encore.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Encore supersedes the original PS3/Xbox 360 release for best-version play and no sourced old-console-exclusive content requires a secondary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Encore is an updated release rather than a remaster; prefer it over the original PS3/Xbox 360 version.

emulation.notes: Run natively on Windows at the highest stable settings.

primary.why: All Out released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and later Nintendo Switch. Windows is the highest-fidelity configurable route, and the Anniversary Edition bundled previously released DLC content on supported platforms.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC version at the highest stable settings with owned DLC or Anniversary content installed; use PS4/Xbox One as console alternatives and Switch only for portable play.

entries.remaster_caveats: Anniversary Edition bundles prior DLC on supported platforms; Switch is a later portable route with technical/content tradeoffs reported in reviews.
